extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computer vision, vision-language models, and multimodal reasoning
extracted.subtask_short: evaluating vlms on visual math problems
extracted.subtask_description: Benchmarking and analyzing vision-language models' ability to solve grade-school math word problems presented in visual/multi-image contexts, including dataset construction and model evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purely visual multi-image mathematical reasoning benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: GSM8K-V, a purely visual multi-image mathematical reasoning benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to address gaps in existing visual mathematical reasoning benchmarks which are often restricted to geometry, lack coverage of math word problems, and rarely assess reasoning across multiple images. The benchmark maps text-based GSM8K samples into visual form to enable evaluation of VLMs on math word problems in visual contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic mapping from text-based GSM8K into visual form
rubrics_metrics.description: GSM8K-V is built by systematically mapping each sample from the widely used text-based GSM8K into visual form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mapping preserves the original problem content while converting it into images (including multi-image cases) so that visual perception plus reasoning is required to solve the problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated image-generation pipeline combined with human annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Through a carefully designed automated image-generation pipeline combined with meticulous human annotation, we curate the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combination of automated generation and human verification/annotation is presented as necessary to produce high-quality visual problem instances; this implies requirements for fidelity, correctness, and clarity of visual renderings and annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality curated sample size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset scale and curation quality are highlighted as criteria — the benchmark is explicitly sized and curated to be a reliable evaluation set for visual mathematical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate a wide range of open-source and closed-source models
rubrics_metrics.description: We evaluate a wide range of open-source and closed-source models on GSM8K-V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarking across diverse model families is implied as a requirement to characterize current capabilities and gaps; comparisons to text-based performance are used for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy as primary evaluation metric (text vs visual comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance comparison example: best-performing model (Gemini-2.5-Pro) achieves 95.22% accuracy on GSM8K but only 46.93% on GSM8K-V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy (percentage correct) is used as a primary metric to quantify model performance degradation from text-based to visual problems; reporting absolute accuracies and comparative drops is part of the evaluation protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze limitations of current models and suggest improvement directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive analysis examining the limitations of current models as well as potential directions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond raw metrics, the benchmark expects qualitative and quantitative analysis to identify failure modes, limitations in perception+reasoning, and suggest directions to improve robustness and generalization of VLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark aims to guide development of more robust and generalizable VLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: GSM8K-V offers a new perspective on visual mathematical reasoning and establishes a benchmark to guide the development of more robust and generalizable VLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset and evaluation protocol should be suitable for driving research toward models that integrate perception and mathematical reasoning across multiple images; suitability for guiding future work is an implicit desideratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage beyond geometry and multi-image reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses gaps: existing visual math benchmarks are often restricted to geometry, lack coverage of math word problems, and rarely assess reasoning across multiple images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid benchmark/sample set should include non-geometry word problems and cases requiring reasoning across multiple images to reflect real-world multimodal mathematical reasoning challenges.
